tasks.title: Add server issue list scope filtering
tasks.description: Implement server-side parsing and validation for issue list scope filters on GET /api/issues. The API should support comma-separated stage selections, the active stage alias, attention=true, and composition with existing priority, label, archived, and all filters.
acceptanceCriteria: GET /api/issues?stage=active returns plan/build/check/integrate issues that are not closed or completed and does not return backlog active issues
GET /api/issues?stage=build,check returns issues whose stage is build or check
GET /api/issues with an unknown stage or alias returns HTTP 400 with a clear error message
Stage selection composes with priority, label, archived=true, and all=true filters using AND semantics outside the stage OR set
GET /api/issues?attention=true returns awaiting-approval, blocked, interrupted, delivery-blocked, integrate-failed, and done-not-merged issues
GET /api/issues?attention=true does not include normal running/probing issues unless another attention condition is present
GET /api/issues?attention=true composes with stage, priority, and label filters
No new workflow stage, status value, or identity model is added
Relevant API/unit tests pass
Typecheck passes
tasks.notes: Keep the query vocabulary server-side. Reuse existing Stage, IssueStatus, isCurrentStageApproval, and classifyMergeDelivery helpers where possible. Do not persist active or attention state.

tasks.title: Expose active and attention filters in CLI list
tasks.description: Update mo issue list to forward comma-separated status selections and the new --attention flag to the server filters from T-001. The CLI should render clear API errors with a non-zero exit code and show a specific empty state when --attention has no results.
acceptanceCriteria: mo issue list -s active sends the active stage alias and displays only returned active pipeline issues
mo issue list -s build,check and mo issue list --status plan,build,check send the comma-separated stage selection without splitting into multiple client requests
mo issue list --attention sends attention=true and displays only returned attention issues
mo issue list --attention with no matches prints a clear attention-specific empty state
Invalid stage or alias errors from the API are printed clearly and the command exits non-zero
CLI help documents --attention, comma-separated --status values, and the active alias
CLI does not add or document a --my flag
Relevant CLI tests pass
Typecheck passes
tasks.notes: This task consumes the server-side list query contract from T-001. Keep mo issue list as a thin client and avoid duplicating attention logic in the CLI.

tasks.title: Add compact issue show mode
tasks.description: Add mo issue show <id> --compact as a single-line human-readable summary mode. Compact mode should use the existing issue detail response, skip long auxiliary fetches, and leave the default show behavior unchanged.
acceptanceCriteria: mo issue show <id> --compact prints one line containing issue number, stage, status, priority, and quoted title
Compact output does not include body, comments, stage checks, approval output, session state, branch metadata, or multi-line warnings
mo issue show <id> without --compact keeps the existing full detail output behavior
Compact mode does not fetch coder sessions or executions
CLI help documents --compact on mo issue show
Relevant CLI tests pass
Typecheck passes
tasks.notes: Reuse CLI command formatting and test patterns established while updating issue list in T-002. Compact is human-readable text, not JSON.

tasks.title: Add API-backed issue diff stat mode
tasks.description: Update mo issue diff to use GET /api/issues/:number/diff for both default patch output and the new --stat mode. Stat mode should print file-level change scale without patch content and preserve the server's merge-base comparison semantics.
acceptanceCriteria: mo issue diff <id> --stat prints file-level additions/deletions and summary counts without any patch hunks or diff --git blocks
mo issue diff <id> without --stat still prints the full patch content returned by the issue diff API
Both default diff and --stat use the same API response and therefore the same base branch, issue branch, and merge-base semantics
not_started, worktree_removed, branch_missing, and git_error unavailable responses render distinct clear feedback and exit non-zero
An available diff with zero changed files renders a clear no-changes message and exits successfully
CLI help documents --stat on mo issue diff
Relevant CLI tests pass
Typecheck passes
tasks.notes: Consume the existing /api/issues/:number/diff response shape. Prefer not to add a stat-specific API unless required by tests or performance constraints.

tasks.title: Add end-to-end CLI regression coverage
tasks.description: Add or extend regression tests that exercise the new issue CLI behavior together rather than only unit-level helpers. The tests should prove the command surface matches the acceptance criteria and that unchanged default behavior remains intact.
acceptanceCriteria: Regression coverage verifies active alias list output excludes backlog active issues
Regression coverage verifies attention list output includes attention items and excludes normal running/probing-only issues
Regression coverage verifies invalid stage input exits non-zero
Regression coverage verifies compact show is single-line while default show remains full output
Regression coverage verifies diff --stat omits full patch while default diff includes patch content
Regression coverage verifies help text includes new options and does not include --my
Relevant test suite passes
Typecheck passes
tasks.notes: This task consumes all implemented command capabilities and closes gaps not covered by focused tests from earlier tasks.
